entry.title: Highway 57 Bakery & Cafe
entry.content:
Butter chicken pie
Tandoori chicken croissant
Apricot almond tartlet
Banana smoothie

When is a banana smoothie not a banana smoothie? When it’s a banana milkshake. We’ve said it before, but clearly it bears repeating - if there is no real banana in your smoothie, it is a milkshake. Today’s beverage was cold, sweet, banana-ey, by all accounts a decent banana milkshake, but a smoothie it was not, no Sir. And they have been penalised accordingly. But this was hardly their only foible.

The pie innards were genuinely boring. Perhaps this is what the everyman wants from a butter chicken pie, but it could at least afford to taste like something. Anything. This was a real shame because the pie crust was sensational, light, flaky, just fantastic. There’s a chance that another pie out of this cabinet could have dragged their overall score up, kicking and screaming, into the good side of average.

The croissant was overall forgettable, they had absolutely squashed it flat to toast it, which made it look a bit funny, but that was the most notable thing about it. And the tartlet was inoffensive but dull. We also look sceptically at any establishment that insists on glad wrapping every single item in their cabinet individually. You just can’t help but wonder how long they have been sitting there when they are all wrapped for maximum freshness and longevity.

entry.title: East Pier Hotel
entry.content:
Bread with dips
Korean chicken
Fried halloumi
Basque cheesecake

East Pier is a sizeable restaurant, the kind of place where they can easily close off a couple of rooms for private events, and is located right on the Ahuriri waterfront. Their prices reflect this. $27 for a mediocre cocktail? $25 for five small pieces of fried chicken? The prices, and the quality, are reflective of a we’re-in-a-plum-spot-and-people-will-come-here-no-matter-what attitude. Admittedly, sitting in the Napier sun on a still August’s day was nice, and the first real sunshine we’ve seen in months (thanks, Wellington). And the food wasn’t bad, but it wasn’t anything you’d make a fuss over. Even trying to think of which dishes were best, or worst, feels a bit redundant, it was all just a forgettable pile of average. Actually, no. We thought that the little coleslaw was a good accompaniment to the halloumi, cutting through the greasiness. The lettuce leaves served with the chicken were a less successful version of the same concept.

entry.title: Afghan Darbar Restaurant & Takeaway
entry.content:
Banjan boranee
Karahi lamb

We dined at Afghan Darbar early in our relationship, before we were keeping BAATFR records. We do not remember it fondly. So when the gods of randomisation brought Afghan Darbar to us again tonight, our emotions were mixed. On one hand, we were quite pleased to see they were still going. Afghani is not a well-represented cuisine in NZ, so we liked that there was support for something different. On the other hand, we were nervous to return to a previous unpleasant dining experience.

Interestingly, the components of the dishes that The Fee-Rex found most pleasant, Business Andy found least pleasant, and vice versa. The Fee-Rex disliked that lamb the most, and found the eggplant kind of indeterminate and smooshy, while Business Andy disliked the mint sauce that was all over the salad, and unfortunately experienced some very thin naan bread.

What we do agree on is that the general ambiance was quite lacking. It was cold for a start, not quite leave-the-doors-wide-open-in-August cold, (looking at you Kaimak Johnsonville), but still cold. The chairs were uncomfortable, and it was awkwardly quiet, so we spent the entire meal listening in to our fellow diners and speculating wildly about their lives.

entry.title: The Realm Hataitai
entry.content:
Chicken burger
Margherita pizza

There is an unspoken rule in hospitality around warning customers about wait times. Some may even call it a duty. An imperative. A mandate. When we walked in and saw two large tables and the rest of the restaurant empty, we weren’t concerned. We saw they had some food and figured we were in the clear. This was reinforced by the waitress saying flat zero about any extended waits.

When we saw more food coming out of the kitchen we thought ooh, this could be for us. But wait, that’s two pizzas. Going to the other table. Then a break. Then two more pizzas. Then a break. And so forth.

Over forty-five minutes we waited. And yes, the blow was softened by their reasonably priced cocktails. But nonetheless, a dereliction of duty has occurred here. Not everybody has 45+ minutes up their sleeve on a Saturday afternoon. At one point, well into the wait, the server said “yours is out next”. It wasn’t. And it wasn’t the food after that either. Did she mean yours is the next table? That’s bloody cheeky phrasing when there’s only three tables here and two have 10+ people.

When the food finally did arrive, one was worth the wait and one wasn’t. The burger was joyful. Structural integrity on point, you could put this thing down and pick it up to your hearts content. The perfect level of spice, crispy hot chicken, just the right amount of salad, and the pickled onion was a nice touch. The margherita pizza wasn’t bad, but it was floppy, over-cheesed, and the crust was chewy.

entry.title: The Original Thai Restaurant
entry.content:
Peanut satay chicken
Thick red curry beef
Roti
Rice

It can be quite intimidating when you realise that you’ve walked into a local fixture unprepared, unknowing, wide-eyed and not expecting to see multiple hugs handed out, several different instances of plans made between customer and proprietor, and promises to return left, right, and centre.

But you also love to see it, it’s like watching wild animals who don’t know that David Attenborough is just over there filming them. You get to see the native Island Bayers in their habitat, free, just living their best lives. Their best lives are at The Original Thai Restaurant and they have been since 1993. Unreal, what longevity. We wondered how they had done it, until we saw the owner just straight vibing with every single patron. We’ve never even noticed this place befoire, but we felt special and valued.

They have a dark secret, however. There’s a minimum charge per person, a minimum charge that is just above the price of almost every dish on the menu. They have upsold almost every single person who walked in the door. But the owner is so friendly, so funny, so energetic, that you leave feeling like it was worth it anyway just to see him do the monkey dance and crack jokes all night.

The food was only okay. Despite winning a Dominion Post award for great value in the year 2000, things have slipped in the intervening 26 years. When the meals came, we thought they were actually pretty small. This, and the $30 minimum charge, were why basically everybody except us ordered both entree and main.

We appreciated being served rice Mum-style from the big silver pot, it gave a lovely friendly vibe. But the flavours were so-so, there was unwelcome surprise pineapple in the chicken dish, and The Fee-Rex got some gristle to boot.

Bookings recommended.

entry.title: Simmer Cafe
entry.content:
Roast vegetable salad
Pumpkin soup
Coffee eclair

At 1 on a Saturday afternoon, Simmer Cafe was pumping. There was one available table, still with the previous diners’ dishes on it, and we had to lunge to it to mercilessly outcompete another couple. But as we have experienced on multiple occasions, popularity does not necessarily correlate with quality.

Let’s start with the positive. The pumpkin soup was fantastic. Really flavourful, seeds on top for texture, beautiful bread, ample butter, and a fair price to boot.

We love roast veggie salad, and it continues to baffle us how so many eateries get this simple dish very wrong. Simmer had ballsed up the veggie selection. Yes, there were some roast veg - carrot, pumpkin, red onion, red capsicum, maybe some kumara. But about half the veg was not roast - mushroom, broccoli, celery, some stringy green thing we’re not even sure what it was. What were these doing in here? Is this a ‘chef’s salad’ situation, where you’re just throwing whatever veggies you have lying around in to use them up? The selection came across as thoughtless. Worse still, they’d drowned it in a honey mustard dressing, then to top it off had poorly heated it so while some was warm, some was definitely not.

The coffee eclair was a disappointment. Call us crazy, but when we order a coffee flavoured pastry, we expect it to taste at least a little like coffee. This was sweet, and had a nicely textured inner cream and top icing, but coffee it certainly was not.

Bookings recommended.

entry.title: 1852 Pub & Kitchen
entry.content:
Cheese pizza
Beef & caramelised onion pizza

“1841 was the year which this great community of ours was settled by Frank Johnson. 1841 Bar and Restaurant is here to bring good old fashioned local hospitality to Johnsonville and the wider Wellington Community.”

Oh, sorry, wrong pub.

“1852 was the year which this great community of ours was settled by John Fitchett. 1852 Pub and Kitchen is here to bring good old fashioned local hospitality to Brooklyn and the wider Wellington Community.”

Did you think we wouldn’t work this out? Upon seeing 1852, we immediately thought it was a sister of that-pub-in-Johnsonville-with-numbers-for-a-name. But then, upon some Googling, there was no apparent link. It wasn’t until we were in the belly of the beast and reading about their copy pasted proud heritage, and browsing their familiar menu, that we made the link. While we could find no actual documentation that these restaurants are the same, they definitely are.

1841 was awarded a 1 in 2024. Normally, a 1 doesn’t get a second chance. Tonight, through deception, they did. And they have risen to the heights of a 2. Admittedly this is a big improvement, but then it would be nigh on impossible to be worse.

We love a bargain. We had initially planned to order one pizza and some nachos, but upon hearing that it was 2-for-1 pizza night, our hands were tied. On the plus side, the pizzas were piping hot with an alright base, and the meat on the pizza was of good quality, no gristly steak here. However, the distribution of pizza sauce was uneven, with some areas of the cheese pizza getting way more than their share. Business Andy had a couple of bites of camembert that he was highly offended by, in fact he used the word ‘ghastly’.

Perhaps they will try to get a third go around, to bring themselves up to a 3. We are on high alert for 1863 lurking for us in another suburb.

entry.title: The Botanist
entry.content:
Breakfast halloumi bao bun
Tofu bao bun
Deep fried cauliflower

This is our third time dining at The Botanist, and our third time complaining about their service. In fairness, the service was better than the previous outings, but there was a service incident which can not go un-discussed. Get a load of this.

We ordered two cocktails with our meal, one espresso martini and one paloma. When the cocktails arrived however, it was two espresso martinis. Easy mistake, no problem. We let them know, and they took one of the drinks away. We could hear them up at the bar saying that there was a mistake, and this espresso martini was meant to be a paloma. We were confident that the paloma would appear momentarily. Then we waited. And waited. The food came. We ate half the food. Then finally the paloma showed up. This is already not great, but what we are about to share with you rocked us to our core. The table next to us was also drinking espresso martinis. The waitress who had removed our mistake-tini took it from the bar to our neighbouring table. And then, within clear ear- and eye-shot of us, said to them “hey do you guys want this espresso martini, it was made by mistake and I’d hate to see it go to waste.” EXCUSE ME? Aren’t we the ones who had the inconvenience of the drink order mistake, and subsequently waited three lifetimes for the correct drink to arrive?? Why would you offer the free drink to some random table, and not to us??? Are these table some kind of VIPs???? Are you worried about “rewarding” us, perhaps suspicious we actually did order two espresso martinis then changed our minds????? Shocking.

Luckily for The Botanist, they make an incredible plate of fried cauliflower. We loved it in 2022, and it stands up gloriously on repeat dining. We eat a lot of fried cauliflower but this was definitely a cut above the rest. The florets were large and meaty, gloriously crisp, so hot, not greasy, a great dipping sauce, and cooked to absolute perfection being neither too hard nor too soft. The bigger the florets, the harder it is to achieve this, so we were very impressed.

The bao buns were acceptable. Their biggest issue was structure, both of them being stacked in a way that made it hard to eat with your hands. So we used knives and forks, but then you’re dealing with issues of mouthful composition. The flavour was a bit same-y between the two, but we appreciated the inventiveness of the breakfast bao offering.

entry.title: Highwater Eatery
entry.content:
Chef’s menu

Congratulations, Highwater Eatery, it’s a pretty big deal to be a four. We award them quite rarely. And it’s really satisfying to go and independently give a four to somewhere that perhaps feels a bit hard done by to not catch a Michelin star recently. Does this mean that actually we’re better reviewers than the fat tire man? We’ll leave the answer of that question up to you.

We’ve said this before, but we’ll say it again. The mark of a great dish is serving you something that you think you don’t like, and showing you how it can be delicious. Neither of us likes mussels, but the mussel emulsion that came with the karaage chicken was outstanding. And that’s not to say that the chicken itself wasn’t incredible too, because it was, but this whole dish came together to become something greater than the sum of its parts. This was the stand out dish of the night, and the field was competitive. We only sampled part of the menu, but there were no fails, and there was plenty more on the menu that sounded similarly good.

And without gushing too much, the dessert was fantastic too. It was a cold apple crumble. If you thought this ws just an apple crumble that was served room temperature, as we did, you’d be wrong. It had been transformed into a whipped, cold sensation that was vanilla-y and delicious. We were entranced.

We could wax lyrical about this meal for a while, but we’ll distill it down. Yum yum yum, try Highwater.

Bookings recommended.

P.S. Extra special shout out to the dude who stuffed his nose into the bucket of cutlery and gave it a giant whiff while we were watching. We still don’t know what this was about, but we have speculated for hours and can only assume it was related to quality control somehow.
